figures.name: 01_native_whole_depth
figures.caption: Curvatures are separated. Different best epochs are descriptive; e300 is the common training endpoint. Histogram spikes include cap point masses.

figures.name: 02_normalized_radius_ecdf
figures.caption: q compares position relative to each ball boundary. Equal q across different curvatures does not imply equal hyperbolic distance or equivalent representation capacity.

figures.name: 03_hier_whole_proxy_depth
figures.caption: V9 HIER whole depth is fixed by construction, not learned. Compare proxies to the HIER view in the same c=0.1 domain; native c=1 whole is a different representation.

figures.name: 04_proxy_parameter_output
figures.caption: The vertical threshold is tangent cap 2.3; output cap depth is 4.6. Selected means hard ancestor usage in the supplied measurement window, not every source of gradient.

figures.name: 05_proxy_id_and_usage
figures.caption: Proxy IDs are aligned within each run, not between independently trained runs. Zero hard selections do not imply zero straight-through or query-endpoint gradients.

figures.name: 06_reverse_nn4_coverage
figures.caption: NN4 coverage is a reverse full-pool retrieval statistic, not a measure of training activation. Equal-depth and angular variants are frozen controls, not retrained models.

figures.name: 07_actual_training_trajectories
figures.caption: Each point uses the stored first training batch (64 positions), before that batch's optimizer step. It is not an epoch-end checkpoint or a clean/eval full-pool distribution. Native curvatures can differ.

figures.name: 08_training_proxy_heatmaps
figures.caption: These are first-batch pre-optimizer proxy states, not epoch-end archive weights. Columns preserve proxy identity within a run. Counts describe only the supplied first-batch selection window.

figures.name: 09_cycle_interim
figures.caption: INTERIM comparison at the same e120 only. The HIER run was still training when collected; this is not its best or final result. Shared c=0.1 does not remove differences from original V9 sampling/seed.

figures.name: 10_checkpoint_proxy_trajectories
figures.caption: These proxy states come from archived epoch-end weights, not first-batch pre-optimizer snapshots in Figures 07-08. Epoch 0 denotes initialization if supplied. Cycle observations are incomplete runs.

figures.name: 11_checkpoint_proxy_heatmaps
figures.caption: Column identity is preserved within each run. Output depth and pre-cap parameter norm are different measurements. Archive time points must not be interpreted as first-batch states of the same numbered epoch.
